context:
Treat this as a typed ingestion problem in BenchBox's ClickHouse-server
client-insert path. Use the corpus logs to select the minimal set of
conversion cases, add targeted tests around the conversion and
schema-introspection helpers, then prove with live representative cells. Fix
DATETIME/TIMESTAMP ordering before DATE-prefix handling, add array parsing,
and harden schema introspection for non-dict schemas. If a benchmark has
invalid source data rather than a loader gap, split that into a
benchmark-specific TODO instead of hiding it in the adapter.
description:
After PR #738 fixed the clickhouse-server provisioning/auth/database/load
path, the 2026-06-01 corpus rerun no longer showed the original 57/57
platform wipeout. The largest remaining failure cluster is server-mode
client-side INSERT type conversion during load, not generic ClickHouse
compatibility.

PR #738 introduced this path because Docker-backed ClickHouse server cannot
read arbitrary host files through server-side `file()`. The path is
BenchBox-side and gated to server deployment mode; clickhouse-local keeps the
faster `file()` load path. The review of the corpus found no silent
corruption: empty strings into String columns are preserved as empty strings,
and every observed type gap fails loudly during load.

Corpus evidence:
  - Matrix: `~/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/uat_clickhouse_server_rc1_corpus_20260601/matrix_summary.tsv`
  - Cells: `~/Developer/benchmark_runs/logs/uat_clickhouse_server_rc1_corpus_20260601/cells.jsonl`

Representative failures:
  - `clickhouse-server_tpcds_0.01_20260601_120433.log`: `Code: 53. Type mismatch in VALUES section... Column c_current_cdemo_sk: required argument is not an integer`; TPC-DS then reports many empty tables.
  - `clickhouse-server_clickbench_1.0_20260601_122208.log`: `ClickHouse file loading failed: 'str' object has no attribute 'tzinfo'`.
  - `clickhouse-server_vector_search_0.01_20260601_133631.log`: `ClickHouse file loading failed: could not convert string to float: '[0.0206561,...]'`.
  - `clickhouse-server_datavault_0.01_20260601_133545.log`: `ClickHouse file loading failed: argument of type 'Table' is not iterable`.

Observed impact from the corpus classifier: roughly 22 of the 42 non-passing
cells are loader type coverage. Bucket A is nullable numeric/date handling
for empty fields into non-Nullable ClickHouse columns (TPC-DS, NYC Taxi,
FlightData, plus downstream TPC-DS OBT). Bucket B is DATETIME/TIMESTAMP
conversion, currently falling through as strings and producing the `tzinfo`
error (ClickBench, H2O DB, TSBS). Bucket C is array/vector parsing for
Vector Search. Bucket D is Arrow/Table-valued schema introspection for
DataVault. These are not platform lifecycle failures: Docker up/down
succeeded and the corpus executed all 57 cells.

anti_patterns.dont: fabricate default numeric/date values for fields that are genuinely nullable.
fix only the first TPC-DS integer column; prove the conversion policy at the helper boundary.
paper over DataVault by special-casing a benchmark name if the bug is schema-object introspection.
restore server-side `file()` loading for Docker-backed clickhouse-server; it cannot read arbitrary host paths.
route DATETIME/TIMESTAMP through date-only parsing; preserve the time component.

Before changing code, drive the conversion/introspection helpers directly
where possible and preserve a compact command/result summary in this
TODO. Raw stdout belongs in `/tmp` or `BENCHBOX_OUTPUT_DIR`, not git.
Expected signatures to re-confirm: empty numeric/date handling, raw
DATETIME/TIMESTAMP string fallthrough, bracketed array/vector parsing,
and Table-valued schema introspection.

RE-VALIDATION (2026-07-16, helper boundary, no Docker). The conversion
helper is benchbox/platforms/base/data_loading.py:
ClickHouseNativeHandler._convert_field_for_clickhouse (landed in the Jul-10
import ded0a94b, AFTER this TODO's 2026-06-01 corpus evidence — the
"Identified" status was stale). Driving the helper directly:
  - Bucket A (empty numeric/date -> NULL): ALREADY IMPLEMENTED and matches
    the ratified policy. `if value == "": return None if
    needs_non_string_value else value`; empty String stays "". No change
    needed.
  - Bucket B (DATETIME/TIMESTAMP): BROKEN. "DATETIME".startswith("DATE") is
    True so `date.fromisoformat("2020-01-15 12:30:00")` raised; bare
    "TIMESTAMP" fell through as str -> driver 'str' has no 'tzinfo'.
  - Bucket C (array/vector): PARTIAL. "Array(...)" parsed, but DuckDB
    "FLOAT[128]" matched the FLOAT branch -> float("[...]") raised.
  - Bucket D (Table-valued schema introspection): crash site FOUND
    statically (no live repro needed) — SchemaInspector.get_column_count
    did `"columns" in table_schema`, which raises `'Table' is not
    iterable` when get_schema returns {name: BaseSchemaTable} (DataVault).
    `_get_column_type_names` separately no-op'd (returned []) for object
    schemas. Both fixed in w2.

work_units.notes:
Keep server mode on client-side INSERT batches for Docker-host files;
do not revert to server-side `file()` loading. Preserve shared ClickHouse
SQL behavior while making type conversion explicit for server inserts.
Implement the ratified nullable-empty-field policy (see open_questions
below): an empty numeric/date value becomes NULL with Nullable(T) DDL
where the reference schema marks the column nullable; NEVER coerce to a
type default. An empty landing in a column the reference schema marks
NOT NULL must fail loudly as a benchmark data defect, not be silently
defaulted.

DONE (Buckets B + C): _convert_field_for_clickhouse now classifies
DATETIME/DateTime64/TIMESTAMP before the DATE prefix and parses to Python
datetime; DuckDB bracketed vector/list types (FLOAT[128], INTEGER[]) route
to array parsing via the new _CLICKHOUSE_VECTOR_TYPE_RE. Bucket A was
already correct (nullable-empty -> NULL, ratified policy) and is unchanged.
All at the helper boundary per anti_patterns; clickhouse-local path
untouched (server-mode-only helper).
DONE (Bucket D): the crash was static, not needing live repro — SchemaInspector.
get_column_count did `"columns" in table_schema`, which raised
`argument of type 'Table' is not iterable` for object schemas (DataVault's
get_schema returns {name: BaseSchemaTable}). Added _schema_table_columns /
_resolve_table_schema helpers that read `.columns` from a BaseSchemaTable
OR ["columns"] from a dict, used by both get_column_count and
_get_column_type_names — so object-schema loads no longer crash AND get
real per-column types (DataVault TIMESTAMP now flows through the Bucket B
fix). All four buckets now handled at code level; only w3 live-cell
verification remains.

Code-review checkpoints to confirm on the live run (from the w2 review):
  - tz-AWARE datetime round-trip: a source timestamp with a 'Z'/offset
    (e.g. TSBS RFC3339) parses to a tz-aware Python datetime;
    clickhouse-driver converts it to the column timezone. Verify the
    stored instant is NOT shifted vs the naive-string benchmarks (a
    non-UTC DateTime column would otherwise corrupt time aggregates). If a
    shift is observed, normalise to naive-UTC before insert.
  - Non-ISO/epoch DateTime formats: datetime.fromisoformat parses only
    ISO-8601, so epoch-seconds or locale timestamps raise (loud, per
    guardrails). Confirm the actual ClickBench/TSBS/H2O timestamp formats
    are ISO; if any emit epoch/other, extend the parser (tracked in
    deferred).
